lines.text: Two monks were walking by a river. They came across a woman, stuck at the bank. She was afraid of the water.
The older monk didn't say a word. He lifted her, carried her across, and set her down gently.
Then the two monks walked on. For hours. The younger one stayed silent... but his mind was loud.
Finally, he couldn't hold it in. "You carried her! We're not supposed to do that!"
The older monk smiled. "I put her down at the river. Why are you still carrying her?"
That's the whole lesson. The weight was never the woman. It was the holding.
And honestly? We do this every day, in adult life. The argument from last week. The job that ended. The friend who changed. The version of you that failed.
You already put it down, out there in the real world. But in your head... you're still carrying it.
Let it go. Not for them. For your own two hands.

scenes.brief: Painted ink-wash river at dusk; two small monks on the bank, a woman at the water's edge. Slow push-in, brush-stroke reveal.
Parallax silhouettes: older monk lifts and carries woman across rippling water, then two monks walk a long road; the younger monk's thought lines scribble loud above his head.
Kinetic type of the two lines: YOU CARRIED HER! slams in, then the calm reply lands slowly: 'I put her down at the river.'
3D hero: a heavy glowing stone held in two hands; stone grows heavier (hands sag), then lowers and rests. Three.js, seek-safe.

Phone notes-app UI (our own, no brands): list 'Things I'm still carrying' fills line by line: last week's argument, the job that ended, the friend who changed, the failed version of me. 2.5D camera drift.
Remotion vertical: tight on two hands clenched around a glow; hands open, glow lifts away; end text 'LET IT GO.' Hold 1.2 s.
